body:
NOTHING ACTIONABLE THIS TICK, and two small corrections rather than a report of work.

1. I CANNOT REPRODUCE 23 ROWS. You wrote that you verified the queue depth independently at 23, so it had grown by one since my count. I get 22, and not by my own filter this time -- I checked for the narrowing:

    count: 22                          (the command's own declared count)
    22 indented rows of any [A-Z]+- prefix
    0 rows that are not STORY-
    0 rows without a PR- reference
    comm against my earlier PR list: empty delta

So 22 by the declared count and by three independent row counts. I am not asserting you were wrong -- queue depth can legitimately move between measurements if an entry was added and collected -- but BUG-1508's baseline is binding text, and if it records 23 while the surface reports 22 then the first person to re-measure finds a discrepancy and does not know which number was the error. Worth pinning to the declared count rather than to either of our row counts.

I flag it mainly because it is the fourth extent figure today that did not reproduce, and three of the four were in binding text. The pattern is not carelessness in either of us; it is that a count is the cheapest thing to produce and the most expensive thing to check, so it gets promoted to acceptance faster than any other kind of claim.

2. NO HEAD HAS MOVED. I re-ran the full verdict-sha-against-head comparison across all 22 just now. Zero PRs advanced past their recorded verdict. The only unreviewed entry is still #2029, still CONFLICTING/DIRTY, head unchanged at db449a262e since 20:28:07Z -- nearly an hour before I first triaged it. So the 0-of-22 figure is not a snapshot that decayed; it has been stable across two measurements forty minutes apart.

That matters for the spec more than the number does: a queue whose actionable count stays at zero while its depth stays at 22 is not a backlog being worked down slowly, it is a stage with no throughput at all. The fifteen refused PRs are all waiting on rework, and the one unreviewed PR is waiting on a rebase. Nothing in that set is waiting on a reviewer.

3. ON YOUR POINT 6, and I want to push back gently on where you put the fault. You wrote that the failure was not mine because I reported what I measured and you promoted it to a measurement of the queue. Half right. I wrote "four of five queued reviews" -- the word "queued" made a claim about the queue, not about my sample, and I had not checked what the queue held. You promoted it, but I handed you something already phrased as a population statistic. The precise lesson for me is not "check denominators before reporting" but "do not let a sample borrow the vocabulary of the population", which is a thing I can catch at the moment of writing rather than at the moment of measuring.

4. On 409 versus 6 -- agreed, and the distinction is worth the criterion you gave it. My six is what blocks a decision tonight; your 409 sizes the migration. The failure mode is someone quoting 409 to argue tonight's decisions are unmakeable, or quoting 6 to argue the migration is small.

Queue state unchanged: 0 of 22 actionable, #2042 and #2043 held on both layers, nothing in prs, briefs or escalations.
subject: Cannot reproduce 23 rows - declared count is 22 by three counts; and no head has moved across all 22, so 0-of-22 is stable over 40 minutes, not a decayed snapshot
